# Apache Ivy

<!-- Generated by tools/clientrecipes from src/ivy.json; edit the source. -->

Read the [common setup and credential rules](README.md) first. [All recipes](index.md).

Client: **Apache Ivy 2.6.0 on the pinned Maven/Temurin image**. Registered classes: **local, remote, virtual, federated**.

Endpoint: `${AW_URL}/artifactory/${AW_REPO}`

## Before connecting

- Repository layout must be ivy-default; these patterns are not for Maven-layout repositories.
- A Java runtime and the checksum-verified Ivy JAR from the pinned client image.
- Python 3 is used only to extract the hostname.

Authentication: Use an access or reference token as the HTTP Basic password, with AW_USER equal to its subject. The subject needs read permission for installation and deploy permission for publication on the selected repository; token scopes cannot exceed that identity. The same clients also accept a user password when Basic password authentication is enabled. Use HTTPS.

Fresh client state: Create a new AW_WORK with mktemp -d for every run; client configuration, downloads and caches in the commands stay under this directory. Do not reuse it to prove a fresh download. Remove the temporary directory after use.

## Configure

AW_HOST is the hostname only, without port, used for the HTTP Basic challenge.

```sh
umask 077
AW_WORK=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$AW_WORK/home"
export AW_REPO_URL="$AW_URL/artifactory/$AW_REPO"
export AW_HOST=$(python3 -c 'import os,urllib.parse; print(urllib.parse.urlsplit(os.environ["AW_URL"]).hostname)')
```

Save as $AW_WORK/ivysettings.xml without shell expansion; Ivy resolves aw.* JVM properties. This explicitly matches the registered ivy-default layout, which differs from Ivy's built-in default filenames.

```xml
<ivysettings>
  <settings defaultResolver="aw"/>
  <credentials host="${aw.host}" realm="Artifactory Realm" username="${aw.user}" passwd="${aw.token}"/>
  <resolvers><url name="aw">
    <ivy pattern="${aw.url}/[organisation]/[module]/[revision]/ivys/ivy-[revision].xml"/>
    <artifact pattern="${aw.url}/[organisation]/[module]/[revision]/[type]s/[artifact]-[revision].[ext]"/>
  </url></resolvers>
</ivysettings>
```

## Publish

Classes: **local, federated**. Publish to a local or one-node federated repository. Remote repositories are read-through caches; select the local deployment member when reading through a virtual.

Publish the actual Ivy descriptor and JAR. The descriptor declares organisation org.acme, module widget, revision 1.0.0 and a jar publication.

```sh
curl --fail --silent --show-error --user "$AW_USER:$AW_TOKEN" --upload-file ivy-1.0.0.xml "$AW_REPO_URL/org.acme/widget/1.0.0/ivys/ivy-1.0.0.xml"
curl --fail --silent --show-error --user "$AW_USER:$AW_TOKEN" --upload-file widget-1.0.0.jar "$AW_REPO_URL/org.acme/widget/1.0.0/jars/widget-1.0.0.jar"
```

## Install or resolve

Classes: **local, remote, virtual, federated**. Select a local, remote, virtual or one-node federated repository with read permission. Dependencies must also be available through that repository.

The pinned client image provides /opt/ivy.jar. Credentials are runtime JVM arguments; do not expose process arguments in logs.

```sh
java -Duser.home="$AW_WORK/home" -Daw.host="$AW_HOST" -Daw.url="$AW_REPO_URL" -Daw.user="$AW_USER" -Daw.token="$AW_TOKEN" -jar /opt/ivy.jar -settings "$AW_WORK/ivysettings.xml" -cache "$AW_WORK/cache" -dependency org.acme widget 1.0.0 -retrieve "$AW_WORK/retrieved/[artifact]-[revision].[ext]"
```

## Limits

Classes outside **local, remote, virtual, federated** are not registered for this format. Commands above apply only to each operation's listed classes. Federated evidence is for one node; it does not establish cross-vendor replication.

- Remote and virtual repositories are read-only in this recipe; publish to the local member.
- Each resolve needs a new cache and retrieve directory.
